subject: stargazer fish
title: This Fish Buries Itself in Sand and Keeps a 50-Volt Shock in Its Head

scenes.text: The scariest thing on this sandy seafloor is the part you can't see.
The southern stargazer shovels itself into sand in seconds, leaving only eyes and mouth showing.
Its eyes sit on top of its head, staring straight up.
When a small fish swims over, it bursts out and swallows it whole.
Grab one, and it has spines above its fins and a pouch behind its eyes that fires up to 50 volts.
Not for hunting. That shock is just to make you let go.

description:
The southern stargazer buries itself in sand in seconds with only its eyes, nostrils and mouth showing, then rises to swallow small fish whole.
A specialised organ in a pouch behind its eyes can discharge up to 50 volts, used to fend off threats rather than to catch prey (Florida Museum of Natural History). Some stargazers also carry venomous spines above their pectoral fins.
Would you step on a sandy seafloor barefoot after this?
first_comment: Spines, a 50-volt shock and it hides under the sand. Which sea creature would you least want to step on?
